projectContext.architectureSummary: Modular monolith with Node.js 20+/Express/TypeScript, PostgreSQL 15 database, Redis 7 cache, JWT authentication, REST APIs with clear service boundaries designed for future microservices migration at scale (100K+ users).

levels.description: Foundation building phase - User Service and Team Service are critical dependencies with high interdependency. Sequential development only to ensure stability.
Stable base established - User and Team services have 90%+ coverage with stable interfaces. Match Service and supporting features can be developed in 2-3 parallel streams.
Mature system - Core services stable with comprehensive test coverage. Stats, League, Tournament services can be developed independently by multiple agents in parallel.

taskSkeletons.title: POST /api/auth/register - User Registration
taskSkeletons.scope: Implement user registration endpoint with email/password validation, bcrypt password hashing, and automatic JWT token generation upon successful registration.
requirements: Accept email, password, name, location in request body
Validate email format and uniqueness
Hash password with bcrypt (12 rounds)
Generate UUID for user_id
Store user in PostgreSQL users table
Return JWT token and user object (excluding password_hash)
Handle duplicate email registration gracefully (409 Conflict)

context.architecturalGuidance: modular-monolith with clear service boundaries in services/user-service/
context.technologyStack: Node.js + Express + TypeScript + PostgreSQL + bcrypt + jsonwebtoken
context.testingApproach: TDD with 90%+ coverage (unit tests for controller/repository, integration tests for route/auth flow, e2e for complete registration flow)

taskSkeletons.title: POST /api/auth/login - User Login

executionStrategy.parallelizationGuidance: Start with P1 (User Service Foundation) sequentially - this is the critical foundation with auth that everything depends on. After P1 maturity gate passes (90%+ coverage, JWT working, all tests passing), proceed to P2 (User Profiles) sequentially to establish stable User Service. After P2 maturity gate passes with 90%+ coverage and stable interfaces, P3 (Team Management) can proceed sequentially. Once P3 is complete and stable, controlled parallelization (2-3 streams) becomes safe for Match Service, Stats Service, and other features. Full parallelization is possible after core services (User, Team, Match) achieve maturity gates.

integrationCheckpoints.checkDescription: Verify User Service auth integration - JWT generation, validation, and refresh token flow all working. Run integration tests against auth middleware with sample protected endpoints.
Verify User Service completeness - all profile CRUD operations working, sports preferences management stable, user search performing well. Run full User Service integration test suite.

Verify Team Service integration with User Service - captain validation working, member validation working, team_members JOIN queries optimized. Run cross-service integration tests (team creation with user validation, member addition with user lookup).

executionStrategy.taskGenerationStrategy: Generate tasks for P1 immediately to start development. After P1 maturity gate passes, generate tasks for P2. After P2 maturity gate passes, generate tasks for P3. This phased task generation allows PM Agent to adjust strategy based on actual maturity progression and learnings from previous phases.

unstructuredNotes:
CRITICAL GUIDANCE FOR TASK GENERATION AGENT AND TASK EXECUTION AGENTS:

1. SEQUENTIAL FOUNDATION IS NON-NEGOTIABLE: P1 and P2 MUST be completed sequentially with 90%+ test coverage before ANY parallelization. User Service is the foundation that everything depends on - do not rush this phase.

2. SPORTS FOCUS: All examples and tests should include pickleball and paddle as primary sports (these are the POC focus). Other sports (basketball, soccer, cricket) should be supported but less emphasized in test scenarios.

3. SOFT DELETE PATTERN: User Service and Team Service use soft deletes (is_active=false, left_at timestamp) to preserve historical data for match integrity. Task Generation Agent should create comprehensive tests for soft delete scenarios.

4. PERFORMANCE WATCH: The user_sports JOIN in profile retrieval and the team_members JOIN in team retrieval are potential N+1 query problems. Task Generation Agent should include performance tests to verify <100ms response times. If performance degrades, consider eager loading or dataloader pattern.

5. SECURITY PRIORITY: Auth vulnerabilities are ZERO TOLERANCE. Task Generation Agent should create comprehensive security tests including SQL injection attempts, XSS attempts, token leakage, timing attacks on password comparison, and authorization bypass attempts.

6. MATURITY GATE ENFORCEMENT: PM Agent will verify maturity gates before proceeding to next phase. If any gate criteria fail, development stays in current phase until all criteria pass. Do not proceed to P2 until P1 gate fully passes.

7. INTEGRATION CHECKPOINTS: After each phase, run cross-service integration tests to verify service boundaries are clean and dependencies are working correctly. This prevents integration issues from accumulating.

8. TASK EXECUTION WORKFLOW: All tasks use TDD workflow (write tests first, then implementation). Task Execution Agents should follow the workflow ref in each task (workflows/tdd.json).

9. FUTURE PHASES: After P3 maturity gate passes, PM Agent will assess readiness for controlled parallelization. Match Service (P4), Stats Service (P5), League Service (P6), and Tournament Service (P7) can potentially be developed in 2-3 parallel streams by specialized Task Execution Agents.

10. HUMAN-IN-LOOP: PM Agent should report phase completion and maturity gate results to Human/Claude for approval before proceeding to next phase. This ensures human oversight of critical progression decisions.
